name: agents-studio
description: Leave Claude Code running — work that fires on a schedule against your own repositories, checks itself with your own tests, and stops when it can't.
author: David Rodriguez Pozo
//: Only the built server and its launcher ship. The build is self-contained — Nitro vendors dependencies into .output/server/node_modules — so an install has nothing to resolve and nothing to compile.
//dependencies: There are deliberately none. Nitro vendors what the server needs into .output/server/node_modules, so a published install resolves nothing, compiles nothing, and does not drag Nuxt and the whole build toolchain onto a machine that only wants to run the thing. The one thing it cannot vendor is the Claude Code CLI: from claude-agent-sdk 0.3 that is a ~290MB per-platform native binary in an optional dependency, resolved at runtime, so the build has nothing to spawn and `server/utils/claudeExecutable.ts` finds the Claude Code the machine already has. Everything below is needed to build it, which makes it a dev dependency by definition. `prepare` rather than `postinstall` for the same reason: postinstall would run on a user's machine and fail looking for nuxt.
